A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same IMBA-loss study. Their complete main text, equations, Figures 1–14, Tables 1–5 and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original controlled experiments, synthetic simulations, benchmark results in Table 3 and appendix ablations in Tables 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulations, benchmark evaluations and appendix ablations, including the numerical outcomes in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same IMBA-distance calculation, token-wise loss weighting and conditional/unconditional training procedure. No model or algorithm component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 31M image-text training corpus, synthetic data and concept-pair scenarios, and evaluate on LC-Mis, T2I-CompBench and Inert-CompBench. Appendix task coverage also matches.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including Baseline and A&E in Table 3, frequency-based weighting in Table 4, sample-wise weighting in Table 5, and SD3/DALL·E3 in Figure 1.

E3.justification: The protocols match, including the 100M–1B model-size sweep, data-distribution ratios, four-epoch benchmark training and evaluation metrics. Appendix B.3 retains its 10K-step fine-tuning procedure and 25 evaluation captions.

E4.justification: The scale/distribution experiments and Appendix B analyses of distance stability, alternative weighting, gamma sensitivity and post-training IMBA distance are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same model-size examples generated from identical initial noise.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate reporting without confidence intervals or significance tests. No repeated-run counts, seed information or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains 62.89% LC-Mis VQA and 57% Inert-CompBench VQA for Ours; Tables 4 and 5 retain the proposed method's success rates of 65.7% and 72%, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), the uniform target concept-distribution assumption, the IMBA-distance derivation in Section 4.1 and Appendix A's formulation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: identifying data distribution as a key factor, proposing online IMBA loss and introducing Inert-CompBench. The added code-access statement does not revise these claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the interpretations concerning model-size saturation, imbalance harming tail concepts and limited fine-tuning gains on inert concepts. Appendix B preserves the same gamma-related color-shift qualification; no substantive limitations or applicability boundaries change.

D1.justification: v2's abstract adds a code-release statement and an explicit GitHub link to KwaiVGI/IMBA-Loss, absent from v1. Implementation details, hyperparameters and pseudocode otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 60 references are unchanged. Neither the claimed novelty nor the relationship to earlier concept-composition and data-balancing research is revised.

P1.justification: v2 updates the affiliation to Kling Team, Kuaishou Technology, adds Yukai Shi's internship marker and footnote, and appends the code-release phrase to the abstract. Section ordering and the scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page additions accompany small spacing and text-flow shifts across the early pages, including moving the start of the Data Distribution paragraph from page 4 to page 3. Figures and tables retain their contents, numbering and designs.

improvement.justification: The new implementation link in v2's abstract modestly improves access to reproducibility resources. The scientific content and appendix evidence remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
